Alexander Hamilton, John Jay, and James Madison, The Federalist Papers.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/alexander-hamilton_john-jay_james-madison/the-federalist-papers

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Alexander Hamilton, author, died 1804 (Wikidata Q178903, death 1804-07-12).
- John Jay, author, died 1829 (Wikidata Q310847, death 1829-05-17).
- James Madison, author, died 1836 (Wikidata Q11813, death 1836-06-28).
- Henry B. Dawson, writer of the introduction, died 1889 (Wikidata Q5717601, death 1889-05-23).
- Henry Cabot Lodge, writer of the preface, died 1924 (Wikidata Q174037, death 1924-11-09).

First publication of the text used: 1787 to 1788, in New York. SE colophon: 'The Federalist Papers were published in 1787 by Alexander Hamilton, John Jay, and James Madison.' Wikipedia (The Federalist Papers): the first 77 essays were published serially in the Independent Journal, the New York Packet, and the Daily Advertiser between October 1787 and April 1788.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in New York between 1787 and 1788, before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United States): the country of first publication is the United States and the text was first published there before 1931, so the US rule settles the origin too, whatever the death years above.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
